The time t required to empty a water tank varies inversely as the rate of pumping p. A pump can empty a water tank in 40 min at the rate of 120 gal/min. Write the equation of the inverse variation. How long will it take the pump to empty the water tank at the rate of 200 gal/min?

t = 4,800/p (k = 40(120) = 4,800); 4,800/200 = 24 min Same structure as quiz item 3 (a time that varies inversely with a rate) but students must decide which quantities multiply to k and write the equation themselves before answering; IXL items are DOK 1-2 and cannot stand in for it. …
Two rectangles both have an area of 144 square units: 72 by 2 and 24 by 6.

A. Sketch as many other rectangles as you can that have the same area. Organize and record your data for the lengths and widths of the rectangles. (1 by 144, 3 by 48, 4 by 36, 8 by 18, 9 by 16, and 12 by 12)
B. Use Structure: considering rectangles with an area of 144 square units, what happens to the width of the rectangle as the length increases? (As the width increases, the length decreases.)

C. Examine at least five other pairs of rectangles, each pair sharing the same area. How would you describe the relationship between the lengths and widths? (In each pair, the lengths and widths are different by reciprocal factors.)
How many length-width combinations for a rectangle can be created from a given pair of factors? → Two; given the factors 2 and 3, a rectangle can have length 2 and width 3, or length 3 and width 2.
Do the lengths and widths always have to be integers? → No; a rectangle with a length of 5 units and a width of 28.8 units has an area of 144 square units.

Sketch as many rectangles as you can that have an area of 25 square units. Is the relationship between the lengths and widths the same as or different from the one for an area of 144 square units? → The same.
Can you write a general equation that models this situation? → xy = k
What would the equation look like solved for the dependent variable y? → y = k/x

nodes.front: Habits of Mind, Use Structure: ask?
nodes.back: How does the formula for the area of a rectangle make sense with the relationships you found? → Area is length times width, so any two factors could be the length and width and give the same product, the area.
